head: f4abd41
block_framing: Neither BLOCK is HTTP-reachable at HEAD: redact_values() has no production call site (verified - only backend/tests/unit/test_log_redaction.py). Both are defects inside backend/src/config/logging.py on the path the repo's own control test test_modules_handling_applicant_pii_enter_a_redaction_scope obliges the next story (E4-S1) to take. A reviewer scoping the gate strictly to 'exploitable through a live route today' would read both as WARN and that reading is defensible. They are recorded as BLOCK because E15-S1 exists specifically so this substrate is correct before anything depends on it, both defects are unfixable by the future caller, and both fixes are local to this diff.

frontend.grading_rationale: devDependencies only; no production artifact ships them; group A deploys no frontend; the critical advisory requires the Vitest UI server and @vitest/ui is not a dependency of this manifest

findings.title: Catastrophic regex backtracking (ReDoS) in the PII redaction pattern
findings.detail: _redaction_pattern joins the escaped characters of the sensitive value with the separator class [\s\-]*. When the value itself contains a separator character (space, tab, hyphen) every literal becomes ambiguous with its neighbouring quantifier and matching degenerates to exponential backtracking. Measured against the real src.config.logging._scrub: a 13-character value ('-'*12 + 'Z') against 40 hyphens of text took 199,326 ms of single-threaded CPU; the same value took 8 ms against 20 chars and 3,125 ms against 30 chars. The sensitive value is attacker-supplied by the module's own documented contract (lines 9-13: per-applicant, per-request data marked by a future origination endpoint), so an applicant submitting a PAN/Aadhaar/salary-document field of '------------Z' chooses the regex. _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH=6 does not help (13 > 6); there is no length cap, character-class restriction or timeout, and _scrub loops over every registered value for every log line in scope.
findings.evidence: measured: value_len=13 text_len=20 -> 8.07 ms; text_len=30 -> 3124.82 ms; text_len=40 -> 199326.11 ms (production _scrub imported directly)
findings.reachability: Not HTTP-reachable at HEAD: redact_values() has no production call site. The repo's own control test obliges the next story (E4-S1, POST /applications) to call it. The defect and its fix are entirely inside this diff.
findings.refutation_attempted: The only refutation found is the absent caller, which is sprint sequencing rather than a mitigation. No sanitiser, length cap, charset restriction or timeout exists between the registered value and the regex builder.
findings.fix: Normalise instead of tolerating separators inside the pattern: strip [\s\-] from both the sensitive value and a normalised copy of the text, match on the normalised form and map back. Minimally: build the separator class only between characters that are not themselves separators, cap the registered value length, and reject values that are predominantly separator characters. Add a regression test asserting _scrub over '-'*12+'Z' against 40 hyphens completes in under 1 ms.
violates: availability of an unauthenticated, unthrottled endpoint (D-O ships no rate limiting)

findings.title: PII in an exception message bypasses redaction and is logged at ERROR
findings.detail: redact_values is a lexical context manager whose finally resets the sensitive-value set. An exception raised inside the scope unwinds that scope first, then propagates past ServerErrorMiddleware, which re-raises it; uvicorn then formats the traceback and logs it on uvicorn.error, by which time _sensitive_values is empty, so the RedactionFilter installed on that logger no-ops. Demonstrated end-to-end against a live uvicorn process running the unmodified application: a handler that entered 'with redact_values(PAN, AADHAAR)' and then raised RuntimeError(f'could not score applicant pan={PAN} aadhaar={AADHAAR}') produced a log line at ERROR on uvicorn.error whose exception field contained 'RuntimeError: could not score applicant pan=ABCDE1234F aadhaar=234123412346' verbatim, with request_id empty. The same values logged inside the scope in the same run were correctly redacted to [REDACTED], so the mechanism works but does not cover the error path. This diff created the sink: f4abd41 routed uvicorn.error through the root JSON handler (line 141) and added payload['exception'] to the formatter (lines 111-117).
findings.evidence: live uvicorn log line contained 'RuntimeError: could not score applicant pan=ABCDE1234F aadhaar=234123412346' in the exception field at ERROR level
findings.reachability: Not HTTP-reachable at HEAD (no PII-accepting endpoint exists). Unlike a normal future-misuse risk, the leak occurs when the caller uses the API exactly as the project's own enforced control test mandates, so a future caller cannot fix it.
findings.refutation_attempted: Rejected three refutations: (a) the RedactionFilter IS attached to uvicorn.error but has nothing registered to scrub by then; (b) the caller cannot hold the scope across the uvicorn boundary because uvicorn logs after the ASGI callable has raised; (c) the caller cannot guarantee no exception message embeds PII, since DB drivers, pydantic and any library raise site are outside its control.
findings.fix: Make the sensitive-value set request-scoped rather than handler-lexical: bind it in CorrelationIdMiddleware (which sits outside ServerErrorMiddleware) and have handlers register into that store so it outlives handler unwinding; and/or catch the exception in the middleware, log it scrubbed while the scope is live, then re-raise. Add a test that drives a raising handler through the real ASGI stack and asserts the PAN is absent from the traceback line.
violates: .claude/claude-security-guidance.md: NEVER log secrets, tokens, passwords, or full PII at INFO level or above
E15-S1-AC1: the captured buffer contains 0 occurrences of each of those three values
E15-S1 scope_out: must not write applicant PAN, Aadhaar or salary-document content to any log sink

findings.title: AppError.context and detail are echoed to the client unfiltered
findings.detail: The handler serialises exc.context (typed Mapping[str, object], i.e. anything) and exc.message straight into the response body with no allowlist, type constraint or disclosure check. Demonstrated live: a 422 returned an envelope whose context carried an applicant PAN, an Aadhaar number, a Postgres connection string including its user and password, a full SQL statement and an absolute filesystem path - all egressed to the client. The probe held an active redact_values scope and it made no difference: redaction covers log records only, never response bodies, so this new outbound channel sits outside the story's PII control. Separately AppError.__init__ defaults status_code=500, so a bare AppError('internal detail') echoes an internal message on a 5xx. Graded WARN because nothing in the diff raises AppError with a populated context and the envelope itself matches the frozen contract (api-contracts.md:27, whose own example legitimately returns the caller's submitted_value); the gap is the absence of any discipline over what may ride out. Class-name disclosure via type(self).__name__ is explicitly mandated by that contract and is not itself a finding.
findings.fix: Give each subclass a declared, typed, disclosure-safe context model (or an explicit public_context allowlist); never place applicant PII, credentials, SQL or filesystem paths in it; for 5xx suppress detail/context and return a generic message plus the correlation id. Add a test asserting a 5xx body carries no detail.

findings.title: X-Request-ID is accepted unvalidated and unbounded
findings.detail: The inbound header is used verbatim with no length cap and no character-class restriction, then echoed into the response header and written into the request_id field of every log line for the request. Verified live: a 64 KB X-Request-ID was accepted, echoed in full (65,692-byte response) and logged in full. /health needs no credentials and D-O ships no rate limiting, so this is a cheap, unauthenticated log-volume and response-size amplifier.
findings.evidence: raw socket: 65536-byte X-Request-ID -> 200 with the full value in the response header and in the access log line's request_id
findings.fix: Cap the accepted value (e.g. 128 characters) and restrict it to [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]; on violation generate a fresh id rather than echoing the caller's.

findings.title: The correlation id is fully caller-controlled, so it can be forged or collided
findings.detail: Any caller can set X-Request-ID to any value, including one identical to another request's id, and every log line for that request then carries it. An attacker can stamp their traffic with a chosen or copied correlation id, merge their requests into another trace, or fragment their own, degrading incident forensics and repudiation. Honouring the inbound header is mandated by the frozen contract (api-contracts.md:19-20, E15-S1-AC3), so the header cannot simply be ignored. Generated ids themselves are sound - uuid4().hex is CSPRNG-backed and not guessable.
findings.fix: Always emit a server-generated request_id on every log line and record the caller's value separately as client_request_id, echoing the caller's value in the response header to satisfy the contract. Validate per SEC-004.

findings.title: The 500 path loses the correlation id on the traceback line
findings.detail: f4abd41 is credited with making the correlation id survive the 500 path; it does for the response header and the truelend.access line, but not for the traceback. Measured in one live failing request: the access line carried request_id 'probe-raise-inside-scope' while the uvicorn.error line carrying the actual traceback carried request_id ''. uvicorn logs after the ASGI callable has raised, by which point the middleware's finally has reset request_id_var. E15-S1-AC3 ('100% of the lines ... each carries request_id equal to req-abc') is therefore not met on the error path, and the repo's own test asserts only the access line, so it passes with the hole open. Primarily a correctness/observability defect; reported here as the forensic half of SEC-002 and because it contradicts the claimed CR-003 fix.
findings.fix: Log the exception from inside CorrelationIdMiddleware while the contextvar is still set, then re-raise; or attach a filter to uvicorn.error that reads a request-scoped store rather than the contextvar.

findings.title: Money wire format is unvalidated, silently coerced, and parsed differently on each side
findings.detail: D-G specifies a quoted 2dp string, but _validate_money accepts anything Decimal() can parse and then silently rounds. Measured on the real types - backend: '1.005'->1.01, '1.004'->1.00, '0.001'->0.00, '-0.001'->-0.00 (negative zero on the wire), '1E5'->100000.00, '1e2'->100.00, '1_000.00'->1000.00, '  1.00  '->1.00, '.5'->0.50, '5.'->5.00, '1.0000000001'->1.00. Frontend decimal.js: '0x10'->16.00 (backend REJECTS it) and '  1.00  ' THROWS (backend accepts it). Three problems: (1) a hostile input yields a monetary value different from the one submitted with no error; (2) exponent, underscore and hex notations bypass any upstream check that assumes plain decimal notation - '1E5' is three characters and means one hundred thousand; (3) the two ends of the wire disagree, contradicting the frontend module's own promise that 'the same amount rounds identically on both sides of the wire'. Not exploitable today (no money-carrying endpoint), but this is the single canonical money wire module for the platform.
findings.fix: Validate against a strict grammar such as ^-?(0|[1-9]\d{0,11})(\.\d{1,2})?$ in _validate_money BEFORE calling Decimal(); reject rather than round anything with more than 2 decimal places; normalise -0.00 to 0.00; apply the identical grammar in toQuantizedDecimal; drive both with one shared fixture set.

findings.title: Money.multiply lets decimal.Overflow escape after ~10 s of CPU
findings.detail: _quantize catches only InvalidOperation and multiply wraps nothing around self._amount * scalar. Python's default decimal context traps Overflow, which is not an InvalidOperation subclass, so it escapes Money's documented error contract. Measured: multiply(10**30) and multiply(10**1000) are correctly rejected as InvalidMoneyAmountError, but multiply(10**1000000) raised decimal.Overflow after 9,690 ms. An oversized scalar therefore both burns ten seconds of CPU and surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a typed validation error. multiply's scalar is an interest rate or term, which on a platform premised on business-configurable loan products without code changes is operator-supplied input.
findings.fix: Bound the scalar's magnitude/digit count before multiplying, and catch decimal.DecimalException (not just InvalidOperation) in _quantize and multiply, re-raising InvalidMoneyAmountError.

findings.title: Frontend money rendering hangs on a pathological exponent
findings.detail: toQuantizedDecimal applies no magnitude bound and MoneyText accepts an arbitrary string. Measured with the project's decimal.js@10.6.0: '1e+1000000' renders a 1,000,004-character string in 41 ms; '1e+100000000' renders a 100,000,004-character (~100 MB) string in 4,825 ms; '1e+200000' through format() takes 16,482 ms for a 266,667-character result, because the thousands-separator regex is super-linear. An 11-byte field value therefore allocates hundreds of megabytes and hangs the tab for seconds - roughly 20,000x amplification. The backend serializer would not currently emit such a value (it always renders 2dp via str(value.amount)), so this needs a compromised or spoofed API response.
findings.fix: Apply the SEC-007 grammar in toQuantizedDecimal, which bounds magnitude, and cap the integer-digit count before toFixed/format.

findings.title: Known advisories in the newly added frontend dependency manifest
findings.detail: npm audit at HEAD reports 5 advisories (1 critical, 1 high, 3 moderate): vitest@2.1.9 critical GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (Vitest UI server arbitrary file read/exec, <3.2.6); vite@5.4.21 high GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff (server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths) plus moderate GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9 and GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3; esbuild@0.21.5 moderate GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99 (any site can query the dev server); @vitest/mocker@2.1.9 moderate GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9. Graded WARN rather than BLOCK despite the raw critical/high labels because all five are devDependencies, no production artifact ships them, group A deploys no frontend, and the critical requires the Vitest UI server while @vitest/ui is not a dependency of this manifest so that path cannot be started. The vite high IS reachable in this project's documented workflow (npm run dev on Windows, the host platform): a malicious page visited while the dev server runs can read files outside the project root - exposure is the developer workstation, not the service. Backend pip-audit is clean.
findings.fix: Bump vite and vitest to patched lines (npm audit fix --force proposes vite 8 / vitest 5 as breaking majors); re-audit before group B ships a deployable frontend.

findings.title: No lockfile is under version control
findings.detail: git ls-files shows no lockfile of any kind. Both lockfiles exist locally but are ignored by .gitignore:48 (*.lock -> backend/uv.lock) and .gitignore:49 (package-lock.json -> frontend/package-lock.json). This diff introduces the project's first dependency manifests, every entry a caret or >= range, so each clone and CI run re-resolves transitive dependencies: a compromised release inside a permitted semver range is installed silently, the set audited in SEC-010 is not reproducible, and no build attestation is possible. The .gitignore rules are pre-existing base state, so the fix touches a file this diff does not own - reported as a conflict rather than proposed as an edit.
findings.fix: Commit frontend/package-lock.json and backend/uv.lock, remove those two .gitignore lines, and use npm ci / uv sync --frozen in CI.

findings.title: extra= fields are silently discarded by the formatter
findings.detail: JSONLogFormatter emits six fixed keys and never reads record.__dict__. Verified: log.info('extra-test', extra={'pan': ..., 'aadhaar': ...}) produced a line containing neither key. Safe today, but extra is dropped rather than redacted - RedactionFilter only scrubs getMessage() and exc_text - so any future change that starts emitting extras would emit them unscrubbed.
findings.fix: Redact at the formatter over the whole rendered payload, or explicitly document that extra= is unsupported.

findings.title: Sensitive values shorter than 6 characters are never redacted
findings.detail: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 silently skips shorter registered values. The stated rationale is sound (a 3-character value with separators tolerated between every character matches far too much unrelated text), but an OTP, PIN, CVV or short account suffix passed to redact_values would go unredacted with no signal to the caller.
findings.fix: Log or raise on a skipped registration so the caller learns the value is not protected.

findings.title: Applicant identifiers persist in a process-global cache beyond request scope
findings.detail: _redaction_pattern is @lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the sensitive value, so up to 256 PAN/Aadhaar values (and their compiled patterns' .pattern attributes) stay resident in process memory long after the request completes, visible in any heap or core dump.
findings.fix: Use a request-scoped cache, or call cache_clear() when the redaction scope exits.

findings.title: URL path segments are logged verbatim, outside any redaction scope
findings.detail: Verified: 'GET /health/ABCDE1234F -> 404' was logged with the path intact. The access line is emitted on http.response.start, after the handler's redact_values scope has closed, so PII in a path can never be redacted. No current violation - the frozen contract uses opaque ids. Query strings are safe: scope['path'] excludes them and uvicorn.access (which would have logged them) is disabled at line 150; verified that a query string carrying pan and aadhaar appeared nowhere in the log.
findings.fix: Keep applicant identifiers out of path segments in every future route, and consider scrubbing the logged path against a request-scoped sensitive set.

findings.title: Redaction coverage is a one-shot enumeration at configure time
findings.detail: _install_redaction_filter_everywhere walks loggerDict once. A logger created later carries no filter of its own and is scrubbed only by the root StreamHandler's filter (confirmed working: a logger created after configure_logging was still redacted). Adding a second handler (file/syslog) without a RedactionFilter would emit unscrubbed records from late-created loggers, and E15-S1-AC2's '100% of configured loggers' holds only at configure time.
findings.fix: Put redaction in the formatter, or install it on handlers only, rather than enumerating loggers once.

findings.title: CR/LF and ANSI injection are blocked only by controls outside this diff
findings.detail: The application performs no validation, but the attack is refuted in the shipped configuration at two independent layers. Verified live: httptools/llhttp rejects CR, bare LF, NUL, ESC and obs-fold in a header value at parse time - all four hostile variants returned '400 Invalid HTTP request received.' without reaching the app - and uvicorn re-validates outgoing header values against [\x00-\x08\n-\x1f\x7f]. Log injection is independently blocked by json.dumps: a payload of quote, brace, comma and backslash metacharacters came back as one valid fully escaped JSON line, and ensure_ascii escapes non-ASCII. No response splitting and no log injection is possible as deployed. Recorded only because the guarantee lives in the server rather than the code: a different ASGI server, an HTTP/2 path, or a proxy that normalises obs-folds differently could re-open it.
findings.fix: Fixing SEC-004 (validate charset and length in the middleware) closes this structurally rather than relying on the parser.

findings.title: GET /health discloses nothing - verified clean
findings.detail: Returns {'status': 'ok'} and nothing else: no version, no config, no dependency state, no secret, no I/O. Unauthenticated access is appropriate for a liveness probe. No remediation required; recorded so the reviewed surface is auditable.
findings.fix: None required. Keep version, build and dependency-state fields out of this body as later stories extend it.

findings.title: Settings holds no secrets and cannot enable debug mode - verified clean
findings.detail: Two non-sensitive fields (service_name, log_level), env_prefix='TRUELEND_', extra='ignore' and no env_file, so no stray environment variable can inject a field and nothing can turn on FastAPI debug (build_fastapi_app never passes debug). Confirmed on the live 500 path: the client received the plain-text 'Internal Server Error' (21 bytes) with no stack trace, no exception type and no internal detail, so the f4abd41 middleware reordering leaks nothing. 'Can a secret reach a log line or the error context' resolves to no because no secret exists yet - re-check when a DB URL or JWT key is added. Minor: log_level is an unvalidated free string, so a bad value raises at root.setLevel on startup (operator-controlled, availability only).
findings.fix: Validate log_level against the permitted set; when secrets are added, keep them out of __repr__/model_dump and out of AppError.context per SEC-003.

findings.title: Framework errors bypass the frozen envelope, and error messages echo unbounded input
findings.detail: Only AppError has a handler. Verified: a 404 returns FastAPI's {'detail':'Not Found'} rather than the contract's {error, detail, context} shape (api-contracts.md:27 requires one shape for every non-2xx response), and pydantic validation errors use {'detail':[...]}. No information leakage in itself, but pydantic reflects the submitted value back in detail, and Money's error messages embed {amount!r} - measured: Money('9'*100000) raises with a 100,024-character message. A 100 KB numeric field therefore yields a ~100 KB error body and a ~100 KB log line, the same amplification family as SEC-004.
findings.fix: Truncate values embedded in error messages (e.g. first 64 characters). Envelope conformance for framework-raised 404/422 responses is a code-review call, not a security fix.
